name: Can custom carpentry conceal utility panels and exposed wall equipment?

mainEntity.name: Can custom carpentry conceal utility panels and exposed wall equipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, finish carpenters routinely build around wall-mounted mechanicals, but building codes require unobstructed access to main panels and shut-off valves. A practical approach is framing removable trim panels, custom cabinet doors, or shadowbox enclosures around electrical breaker boxes, irrigation controls, and central vacuum units. This keeps the garage looking neat and fully finished while allowing immediate, tool-free access whenever an electrician, plumber, or utility inspector needs to service the equipment.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, carpenters can build flush access panels or custom cabinet fronts that conceal equipment while maintaining code-compliant, unobstructed access to utilities.
